security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false matches in font licenses, Markdown, examples, tests, and structured coverage data. Two findings are confirmed because shadcn_add.py invokes npx with project-sourced version data and unvalidated component arguments. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The component installer executes npx with a project-sourced version and unvalidated component arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Require an exact semver, reject option-like component names, add an explicit approval preview, and document that the command downloads code and changes project files.

content.value_statement: Building consistent, responsive interfaces requires many component, styling, and accessibility decisions. This skill provides shadcn/ui patterns, Tailwind guidance, and focused automation.
actual_capabilities: Select and compose shadcn/ui components for forms, navigation, dialogs, tables, and feedback.
Apply Tailwind utilities for layout, spacing, typography, color, borders, and shadows.
Design mobile-first responsive layouts with breakpoints and container queries.
Implement themes, dark mode, CSS variables, and reusable design tokens.
Apply keyboard, focus, screen reader, motion, and form accessibility patterns.
Generate Tailwind configuration and install shadcn/ui components with included Python tools.
limitations: Most component guidance targets React frameworks and shadcn/ui conventions.
The skill does not render previews or verify visual results automatically.
Accessibility guidance still requires browser, keyboard, and screen reader testing.
The installer requires Node.js and npx, may use the network, and changes project files.

use_cases.title: Build a Product Dashboard
use_cases.description: Create responsive dashboard layouts with accessible cards, tables, filters, dialogs, and clear loading states.

use_cases.title: Standardize Interface Tokens
use_cases.description: Define colors, spacing, typography, breakpoints, component variants, and dark mode across an application.

use_cases.title: Translate Designs into Components
use_cases.description: Turn interface requirements into reusable shadcn/ui compositions with responsive Tailwind styling and accessibility behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Style One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Style a [component] with shadcn/ui and Tailwind. Include accessible states, responsive behavior, and a concise explanation of key choices.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Responsive Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mobile-first [page type] for [framework]. Use shadcn/ui, define breakpoint behavior, and include loading, empty, error, and success states.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Theme System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Tailwind theme for [brand]. Define semantic color tokens, typography, spacing, dark mode, focus styles, and component variant guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Refactor an Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the provided interface for accessibility, responsive layout, theme consistency, and component composition. Prioritize issues, then propose focused shadcn/ui and Tailwind changes.

output_examples.input: Create an accessible account settings form that works on mobile and desktop.
output: A responsive form structure using labeled shadcn/ui controls.
Inline validation, focus management, disabled states, and clear submission feedback.
A single-column mobile layout that becomes a structured desktop settings view.

output_examples.input: Define a dark mode theme for a data-heavy analytics product.
output: Semantic tokens for surfaces, text, borders, status colors, and chart accents.
Dark mode values with readable contrast and restrained elevation.
Guidance for tables, filters, dialogs, focus rings, and selected states.

output_examples.input: Improve a card grid that overflows on small screens.
output_examples.output: A mobile-first grid plan with stable gaps, constrained content, responsive columns, and long-text handling.

best_practices: Start with semantic HTML and accessible component behavior before visual refinement.
Use shared tokens and responsive constraints instead of isolated values and viewport-specific fixes.
Test keyboard navigation, focus visibility, contrast, reduced motion, and content overflow at representative sizes.
anti_patterns: Do not remove focus indicators or rely on color alone to communicate state.
Do not build class names dynamically when Tailwind cannot discover them during compilation.
Do not run the component installer without reviewing the resolved command and expected file changes.

faq.question: Which frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance primarily supports React frameworks such as Next.js, Vite, Remix, and Astro, with Tailwind patterns useful elsewhere.

faq.question: Does this skill require shadcn/ui?
faq.answer: No. Tailwind layout, responsive design, theming, and accessibility guidance can be used without shadcn/ui.

faq.question: Can it add components automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The included Python installer wraps npx shadcn, requires an initialized project, and should be reviewed before execution.

faq.question: Can it generate Tailwind configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. The configuration tool supports framework paths, colors, fonts, spacing, breakpoints, and recommended plugins.

faq.question: Does it guarantee accessibility compliance?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns, but compliance requires testing with browsers, keyboards, assistive technology, and relevant standards.

faq.question: Does it create finished visual assets?
faq.answer: It provides canvas-oriented design guidance and interface patterns, but it does not include a renderer or image generation engine.
